disagreements.topic: 2028 EPS base and the MarketScreener share count
disagreements.positions: Agent_1 uses EUR 60.5 net of MATCH (gross 62.7 on 378M shares), agent_2 EUR 60 (sales EUR 63B, below consensus), agent_3 EUR 59.8 (sales EUR 61B, ~6% below consensus), agent_4 EUR 61 (gross 62.9 on 372M shares), agent_5 EUR 59.5 net (gross 62). Agents 1, 2, 4 and 5 all say MarketScreener's EUR 68.32 implies only ~357M shares.
disagreements.resolution: Settled on the facts; the remaining gap is judgment. MarketScreener's table has 2028 net income of EUR 24.36B, which divided by EUR 68.32 EPS gives 356.5M shares. Its own 2027 line implies 373M, and its stated share count is 384.05M. ASML's buyback runs at about EUR 1.1B a quarter (Q2-26 6-K) under the EUR 12B 2026-28 program, and up to 2M of those shares go to employee plans. That gives about 379M shares at end-2027 and about 376M on average in 2028, not 357M or 372M. On a consistent share count, consensus 2028 EPS is about EUR 64.8 gross (EUR 24.36B / 376M), or about EUR 62.2 after a ~4% MATCH haircut. All five agents sit 2-4% below that. Agents 2 and 3 do so on purpose: the 2028 capacity step is still 'under investigation', the consensus range is wide (EUR 53-68), and MarketScreener's page is dated 2026-01-28. That is a defensible haircut, not an error. Moving to consensus would add about 2% to NTM EPS, roughly 1-1.5 points at mid strikes, which is about the size of the unpriced post-run-up drift penalty in agent_5's base rates. I leave the ladder at the mean.
disagreements.evidence: MarketScreener ASML finances table (net income 2027 EUR 19.5B / 2028 EUR 24.36B; EPS 52.29 / 68.32; FCF 16.7B / 20.48B; data date 2026-01-28); ASML Q2-26 6-K (buyback ~EUR 1.1B in Q2); ASML Q4-25 release (EUR 12B program to end-2028, up to 2M shares for employee plans).

disagreements.topic: FCF per share and the FCF yield in the cash-flow leg
disagreements.positions: 2028E FCF/share: agent_1 EUR 54.5 at 3.35%; agent_2 EUR 55.7 at 3.35%; agent_3 EUR 18.9B (~EUR 50.3/share) at 3.0%; agent_4 EUR 48.9 at 2.9%.
disagreements.resolution: Partly settled. Consensus 2028 FCF is EUR 20.48B, about EUR 54.5/share on 376M shares, an 84% conversion of consensus net income. Agent_1 matches it. Agent_4's EUR 48.9 is about 10% below consensus, but its lower 2.9% yield offsets that, so its leg ($1,897) ends up close to the others ($1,827-1,884). The spread in this leg comes from the yield chosen, not from a factual error, and nets out across the agents.

disagreements.topic: Odds that the MATCH Act is enacted in the December NDAA
disagreements.positions: Agent_1 35% (3.5% EPS haircut); agent_5 40% (4%); agent_3 ~50%; agents 2 and 4 give no explicit probability but put it in the bear case at 20-23%.
disagreements.resolution: Not settled. Nothing new since the round-1 check. A stronger MATCH text is in the Senate manager's amendment, and the four-corners text can go around a Senate floor vote. The Senate returns the week of 11-09, and outside groups are now lobbying conferees on the AI/export provisions. The 35-50% range is reasonable and nothing published supports a narrower one. Expected cost is about 3.5-5% of 2028 EPS, which is already in every agent's numbers. The event falls outside the 1-month window.
disagreements.evidence: Punchbowl / Sen. Banks 'Chips bills poised for NDAA ride'; AIPN FY27 NDAA conference letter; round-1 checks (CRS IN12704, ndaa.ai).

disagreements.positions: Agent_5 puts 40% weight on 34x CY2027 EPS and 10% on the mean analyst target of $2,116. Agents 1-4 capitalize NTM EPS at 27.5-28.5x and blend in an FCF yield.
disagreements.resolution: Methodological, not factual. At the horizon, 34x CY2027 EUR 51.73 is the same price as ~29.5x NTM, so it is not double-counting. But it is the highest horizon multiple of the five, a full turn above the others under a hiking Fed. The analyst-target leg restates sell-side consensus rather than adding independent evidence. Agent_1 sits at the low end mainly because it uses 90% FCF conversion and a 3.35% yield. With both ends kept, the agents' mean of $1,876 is a fair centre. My own check gives about $1,860-1,880: NTM EUR 59 x 28x x 1.1243 = $1,857, and FCF EUR 54.5 / 3.3% x 1.1243 = $1,857, with a small lift if 2028 moves to share-neutral consensus.

Kept at $1,200, the agents' mean and the round-1 level. $1,150 to $1,250 is 20-21.5x CY2027 consensus. Agents 1 and 4 argue that a sentiment and rates selloff like 09-08 to 09-14 (-11% in four sessions) could reach the $1,200s without fundamental damage. But that would take another ~25% fall from the September low, which a pacing scare alone has not produced this cycle.
disagreements.evidence: Twelve Data daily (low close $1,575.15 on 2026-09-14); consensus EUR 51.73.

disagreements.positions: All five have Q3 on 10-14 and an FOMC in late October; agents 2, 3, 4 and 5 give 10-28; agent_4 dates Micron's print to 10-01.
disagreements.resolution: Settled. ASML Q3 results come out 2026-10-14 before the open. The FOMC meets 10-27/28, decision 10-28 at 2pm ET, with no SEP. Micron reported FQ4 on 2026-09-30 after the close: revenue $54.2B, with FY27 capex to rise. 10-01 was only the trading reaction. MarketBeat's Q3 consensus of '$12.54 EPS on $13.18B' is a USD series that does not match EUR 10.65 / EUR 11.68B at spot FX (that would be $11.97 / $13.13B), so the EUR figures from the primary guide and Yahoo should be used. One search result showed a MarketBeat 'actual EPS' for 10-14. That date is after the as-of date, so I ignored it and did not use it.
disagreements.evidence: MarketBeat earnings page; Federal Reserve October 2026 calendar / fedratecalc; Micron FQ4-26 8-K (2026-09-30); CNBC 2026-09-30.

one_month_reasoning: The window events are confirmed. Q3 reports on 10-14 before the open: the guide is EUR 11-12B at 55-57% GM, consensus is EUR 10.65 EPS on EUR 11.68B, and the reaction will turn on the first 2027 commentary and H2 cash conversion. TSMC reports around 10-15, and the FOMC decides on 10-28 without an SEP, with markets leaning toward a hold. Micron's 09-30 beat and higher FY27 capex is already in the price. MATCH cannot be decided before the Senate returns around 11-09. All five agents now centre on spot at a 13.5-14% monthly sigma, I found nothing that gives a directional edge, so I keep their mean.
confidence_reason: In round 2 the forecasts converged to within 8 points at every strike (P(>=spot) 0.48-0.56), and every round-1 factual error has been fixed. This round's checks confirmed the catalyst dates and settled the share count and FCF facts behind the 2028 base. The one lever left is that agents sit 2-4% below share-neutral 2028 consensus, which is worth about 1-1.5 points at mid strikes. That is a judgment about a dispersed, January-dated consensus, offset by near-zero post-run-up base rates, not a settled error. So I leave both ladders at the mean.
thesis_break_reason: $1,200 is about 20.6x CY2027 consensus (EUR 51.73 = $58.2) and about 18x horizon NTM EPS (~EUR 59 = $66). It sits below the March-2026 low (~$1,248) and 24% below the 2026-09-14 close of $1,575.15, the low of a sentiment-only AI-pacing selloff. A sustained close there would most likely mean fundamental damage: a December NDAA that enacts MATCH's DUV sales and servicing ban without a Dutch carve-out, 2027-28 EUV slot push-outs or a memory capex reversal, or a weak 2027 guide in January 2027. It is the mean of the agents' $1,150-1,250 range.
key_drivers: Earnings base: 2027 consensus EUR 51.73 (~$58; ~31x today) on EUR 54.6B sales, backed by ~85 low-NA EUV units of 2027 capacity described as close to fully covered. 2028 consensus is EUR 65.0B sales and EUR 24.36B net income, or about EUR 64.8 per share on a consistent ~376M shares (MarketScreener's EUR 68.32 implies an impossible 357M). The agents capitalize EUR 59.5-61 after MATCH risk.

Horizon multiple: 27.5-29.5x NTM in Oct-2027 under a Fed that hiked on 2026-09-16 and may hike again in December. Pooled ASML/LRCX/KLAC base rates after >+60-80% run-ups show a forward-12m median of only +1% to +7%.

MATCH Act in the December FY27 NDAA four-corners text: 35-50% enactment odds, an expected cost of ~3.5-5% of 2028 EPS, and the main route to the $1,150-1,200 bear case (China ~20% of FY26 sales, including servicing).

Memory/AI capex durability into 2028: Micron FQ4-26 revenue of $54.2B with higher FY27 capex and TSMC 2026 capex raised to $60-64B support it. Against that, DRAM contract growth is slowing (TrendForce 4Q26 +10-15%) and Korea was 43% of Q2 system sales.

Cash conversion and buyback: H1-26 FCF of about EUR -1.3B on a receivables build. Consensus expects FCF of EUR 16.7B (2027) and 20.5B (2028), about 84% of net income. The EUR 12B buyback runs at ~EUR 1.1B a quarter.

fair_value.reason: Horizon NTM EPS of ~EUR 59 (0.25 x 2027 EUR 51.7 + 0.75 x 2028 ~EUR 61.5, between the agents' 59.5-61 and share-neutral consensus net of MATCH, EUR 62.2) x 28x x 1.1243 = ~$1,857. Consensus 2028 FCF of EUR 20.48B / 376M shares = EUR 54.5 at a 3.3% yield = ~$1,857. A modest weight on the share-neutral consensus lifts the blend to ~$1,875, which equals the agents' mean ($1,876). Agent_4's FCF/share (EUR 48.9) and share count (372M) and MarketScreener's implied 357M are corrected, but these errors net out.

summary: After round 2 the five forecasts sit close together: P(close >= $1,808 on 2027-10-01) is 0.48-0.56, fair values are $1,813-1,975 with a mean of $1,876, and every round-1 factual error has been fixed. I keep both ladders at the mean: median about $1,820, about +1%, against ~42-46% vol. The remaining disagreements are judgment calls: how far below the share-neutral 2028 consensus (~EUR 64.8; MarketScreener's EUR 68.3 uses an impossible share count) to set EPS, a 27.5-29.5x horizon multiple under a hiking Fed, and 35-50% odds that the December NDAA carries the MATCH Act. Near-term events are Q3 on 10-14 and the FOMC on 10-28; the big binary event is the December NDAA text. Thesis break is $1,200.

sizing.reason: The checked fair value (~$1,875) is only ~4% above spot, and the median 12-month outcome is about +1% at ~42-46% vol. To beat SPY on Sharpe the stock would need roughly three times SPY's excess return, which the evidence does not support. The name would be a fourth AI-capex holding and carries a binary December NDAA/MATCH event, so I cap it at 5%. Liquidity and listing age are not concerns.
